papers.source_edition: Nature Human Behaviour Version of Record / complete official article HTML, published 2023-10-16
papers.central_mechanism: Bayesian-symbolic conceptual bootstrapping using adaptor-grammar cache/reuse, combinatory-logic program structure, and a dynamically updated latent concept library under bounded search.
papers.determination: The paper explicitly says that it adapts the algorithm of Liang, Jordan & Klein (2010). The inherited operator is the combinatory-logic/adaptor-grammar program-sharing and cache/reuse machinery; CNC-01 changes it into a process-level conceptual-bootstrapping model with a dynamic latent concept library.

direct_edges.mechanism: combinatory-logic program representation plus cache/share/reuse inference machinery used as the basis of the dynamic concept-library process model

bounded_non_direct_notes: Liang 2010 itself builds on combinatory logic and hierarchical nonparametric Bayesian sharing; these are constituent intellectual ancestors, but W8-A does not invent transitive direct CNC-01 edges to them.
DOI absence no longer makes this ancestry underdetermined because the predecessor is uniquely identified by exact proceedings metadata and stable ICML/DBLP records.

papers.source_edition: Computational Brain & Behavior Version of Record / complete official Springer HTML, published 2023-12-28; volume 7, pages 129-149 (2024)
papers.central_mechanism: The inherited ACT-R declarative-memory operator family: activation B+S, trace/base-level decay, spacing-sensitive trace decay, retrieval competition/partial matching, and reconstructive blending.
papers.determination: The paper is not constructing an unrelated memory model; it explicitly analyzes ACT-R declarative memory inherited across prior ACT-R work. Exact source-level origins can be bounded without reconstructing all ACT-R history.

direct_edges.mechanism: ACT-R declarative-memory algorithmic implementation used as the paper's operative formalism
base-level activation power-law trace accumulation reproduced as equation 3
trace-specific decay modification used in equations 4-5 to obtain spacing effects
ACT-R blending mechanism used for reconstructive aggregate retrieval and equation 8

bounded_non_direct_notes: Anderson, Reder & Lebiere 1996 is a source-backed ACT-R constituent for source activation and partial matching, but MEM-01 does not locally attribute equation 7 to it as a unique origin; W8-A records SHARED_CONSTITUENT rather than manufacturing an exact direct edge.
Anderson et al. 2004 is a source-backed ACT-R architecture reference and is kept as SHARED_FRAMEWORK.

A non-DOI book node is not required for this bounded resolution: Anderson 2007 has a verified book-level DOI. A non-DOI proceedings node is nevertheless scientifically necessary because the paper explicitly attributes blending to Lebiere 1999.

papers.source_edition: PNAS published article / official PNAS-PMC full text, 1998-11-24, volume 95(24), pages 14529-14534
papers.central_mechanism: Long-range recurrent global-workspace gating with reward/vigilance modulation and reward-modulated synaptic update in an effortful-task architecture.
papers.determination: The 1998 paper explicitly states that its minimal scheme extends four earlier Dehaene/Changeux task models (delayed response, card sorting, numerical processing, planning) and specifies a common architectural principle. The exact cited editions and DOI edges can therefore be represented without relying on shared authorship.

direct_edges.mechanism: predecessor delayed-response neuronal model; reward-modulated Hebbian and reward-linked stability mechanisms are explicitly referred back to this model
predecessor card-sorting neuronal model within the explicit four-model extension family; also cited for reward-linked short-term stability
predecessor number-processing neuronal model named in the explicit extension statement and unified by the common architecture
predecessor planning neuronal model; reward-linked workspace stability mechanism is reused and generalized

bounded_non_direct_notes: The direct edges are admitted because the descendant itself says the scheme extends these named prior task models; same authorship is not used as evidence.
No additional earlier transitive lineage is promoted unless each intermediate relation is separately source-supported.

papers.source_edition: PLOS Computational Biology Version of Record main article plus the already-frozen official supplement bundle; published 2010-04-29
papers.central_mechanism: Spiking-neuron task-set router with NMDA-mediated recurrent integration, accumulation-to-threshold response gating, inhibitory reset, and sensory buffering.
papers.determination: INT-06 explicitly says that the model capitalizes on existing elements but that the novel contribution is their integration into a global functional architecture. Exact implementation descent is source-explicit for the local recurrent module/parameters and the motor threshold circuit; this does not license a direct edge to INT-03.

direct_edges.mechanism: local sensory/router recurrent module and synaptic efficacies; INT-06 states that local efficacies are the same as this predecessor
motor response selection and cortico-basal-ganglia threshold-detection circuit explicitly modeled from Lo & Wang

bounded_non_direct_relations.mechanism: recurrent decision/integration module family used among prior local-module studies
reciprocal/feedback recurrent workspace-style modulation cited as a previous model, not an exact descendant identity
inhibitory reset is described as similar to the predecessor's termination signal
same broader Dehaene workspace/recurrent lineage, but INT-06 does not source-explicitly claim descent from the 1998 INT-03 model and its central task-set/NMDA router is a distinct implementation

bounded_non_direct_notes: The phrase 'capitalizes on existing elements' is not converted wholesale into direct ancestry; direct edges are limited to loci that say the implementation/parameters are modeled as or the same as a predecessor.
INT-03 ↔ INT-06 remains a shared-framework relation, not a direct model edge.
